items.title: 61426_Jacques Butler oral history interview
items.q: the man liked me, he allowed me to call him Preacher. He was one of the most dignified men I've known.

ctx.x: And somebody asked them -- a razor blade, wanted to cut the other one's face or something and the other one was off there looking for, I think, a hunting knife and so I saw that.

Then, that was all right, they kind of settled that but everybody was ill at ease and there was a man his name was -- great singer -- I called him Preacher. And the man liked me, he allowed me to call him Preacher. He was one of the most dignified men I've known.

I'll get his name later. So, he would open the show, he would open the show and sing There'll Always be an England and that was it. When he started marching on that cane, that was all that had been written.
